calls.head: Rovers on the blue line vs. Stay-at-homes
calls.body: The Oilers’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Edmonton is near the top of the league for shots from defensemen, and Minnesota is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Oilers’ defensemen jump into the play.
calls.call: The Oilers’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Wild’s.

surprises.body: Minnesota’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Bouchard ends it in overtime
paras: Joel Eriksson Ek opened the scoring for the Wild early in the first. Leon Draisaitl made it 1-1 for Edmonton on the power play with just three seconds left in the period. Draisaitl struck again on the power play early in the second to put the Oilers ahead 2-1, his fourth straight game with a goal. Mathieu Joseph made it 3-1 just under five minutes later. Kirill Kaprizov pulled the Wild within one midway through the third, his fourth straight game with a goal. Ryan Hartman tied it 3-3 with just under seven minutes left. Evan Bouchard won it on the power play in overtime. Connor McDavid finished with three assists.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Devon Levi made 27 saves for the Oilers, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 28 of 32 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Quinn Hughes had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Bouchard’s overtime winner in the game.
The Oilers went 3-for-5 on the power play. The Oil moved to 7-1-1, still first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Wild fell to 6-2-2, second in the Central.

items.text: Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
Quinn Hughes extended his point streak against Edmonton to seven games.
Ryan Hartman scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 9 (ten games played since).

The Wild were without Jared Spurgeon, Marcus Foligno, Olli Määttä and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Sabres were missing more at the time.
